intro: Iowa runs its elections county by county, through each county auditor, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Show an Iowa driver's license or non-operator ID, a U.S. passport, a U.S. military or veteran ID, a tribal ID, or an Iowa Voter ID Card, which is free from your county auditor. If you have none of these, you can prove who you are and where you live with Election Day registration documents or vote a provisional ballot.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Absentee voting in person
dates.detail: Vote in person at your county auditor's office. County auditors can also start mailing absentee ballots on Oct. 14.

dates.label: Last day to pre-register to vote
dates.detail: The pre-registration deadline is 15 days before the election. You can also register at your polling place on Election Day, if you show proof of who you are and where you live.

dates.label: Mailed absentee request must be received
dates.detail: Your county auditor must have your written request by 5 pm. Any registered voter can ask for an absentee ballot.

src.label: Iowa Secretary of State — plan to vote, 2026 general election

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. An absentee ballot must be back at your county auditor's office by 8 pm.
